markers.label: Pristina
markers.description: Kosovo's lost autonomy, parallel institutions, and police control centered political pressure in Pristina.

markers.label: Drenica
markers.description: Drenica became a KLA stronghold and one of the first major zones of Serbian security operations.

slides.title: Origins and Road to War
slides.cap: Visual reference for Origins and Road to War.
slides.body: The Kosovo War grew from the loss of Kosovo's autonomy, Serbian police control, Albanian parallel institutions, failed nonviolent resistance, and the rise of the KLA. By 1998, repression and insurgency had made compromise increasingly unlikely.

stats.val: Origins and Road to War

markers.label: Drenica region
markers.description: Serbian operations in Drenica radicalized the conflict and expanded support for armed resistance.

slides.title: Drenica massacres
slides.body: The Drenica massacres radicalized the conflict. Serbian operations against KLA-linked areas killed civilians and helped transform the KLA from a marginal armed group into a wider symbol of resistance.

stats.val: Drenica massacres

markers.label: Prekaz
markers.description: The attack on the Jashari compound became a founding martyrdom story for the KLA.

slides.title: Attack on Prekaz
slides.cap: Visual reference for Attack on Prekaz.
slides.body: The attack on Prekaz killed Adem Jashari and many members of his family. For Kosovo Albanians, it became a martyrdom story that increased recruitment and hardened the war's emotional stakes.

stats.val: Attack on Prekaz

markers.label: Račak
markers.description: Račak shifted international diplomacy by making civilian killing impossible to treat as a local security incident.

slides.title: Račak massacre
slides.body: The Račak massacre became a diplomatic turning point. International observers treated the killings as evidence that the conflict could not be contained by negotiations alone.

stats.val: Račak massacre

markers.label: Belgrade
markers.description: NATO struck Yugoslav command, infrastructure, and military targets to force withdrawal from Kosovo.

markers.label: Kosovo front
markers.description: The air campaign coincided with intensified expulsions and violence on the ground.

slides.title: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia
slides.cap: Visual reference for NATO bombing of Yugoslavia.
slides.body: NATO's bombing campaign aimed to force Yugoslav withdrawal from Kosovo after diplomacy failed. The air war changed the strategic balance but also coincided with mass expulsions and civilian suffering on the ground.

stats.val: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia

markers.label: Izbica
markers.description: Izbica became one of the massacre sites later documented by human-rights investigators.

slides.title: Izbica massacre
slides.body: Izbica became one of the documented massacre sites of spring 1999. It showed how village-level killings formed part of a wider campaign of expulsion and terror.

stats.val: Izbica massacre

markers.label: Meja
markers.description: Meja was one of the largest single massacres of Kosovo Albanian civilians during the war.

slides.title: Meja massacre
slides.body: The Meja massacre was one of the largest killings of Kosovo Albanian civilians during the war. It remains central to memory, missing-persons work, and accountability efforts.

stats.val: Meja massacre

markers.label: Ćuška / Qyshk
markers.description: Ćuška marks the Peja-area violence and the broader pattern of expulsions, killings, and cover-up.

slides.title: Ćuška massacre
slides.body: The Ćuška massacre belongs to the Peja-area pattern of killings, expulsions, and property destruction. It shows how the war's violence moved through villages and family networks, not only formal battlefields.

markers.label: Pristina Airport
markers.description: Russian troops' arrival at the airport exposed the diplomatic tension behind the postwar NATO-led deployment.

slides.title: Incident at Pristina Airport
slides.cap: Visual reference for Incident at Pristina Airport.
slides.body: The Pristina Airport incident exposed postwar great-power tension. Russian troops reached the airport before NATO, creating a brief standoff over who would shape Kosovo's security order.

title: International and Human Dimensions
sub: The wider impact of the Kosovo War

markers.label: Kukës refugee route
markers.description: Hundreds of thousands of refugees crossed into Albania during the expulsions.

markers.label: North Macedonia border
markers.description: Another huge flow of refugees crossed south toward Macedonia.

slides.title: International and Human Dimensions
slides.cap: Visual reference for International and Human Dimensions.
slides.body: The war produced mass displacement, refugee columns into Albania and North Macedonia, NATO intervention, Russian diplomacy, and UN administration. Civilians were the central victims of expulsions, massacres, airstrikes, and reprisal attacks.

title: Outcome and Legacy
sub: How the Kosovo War ended and what followed

markers.label: Pristina
markers.description: Kosovo came under UN administration after Yugoslav withdrawal.

markers.label: Mitrovica
markers.description: Mitrovica became a symbol of the unresolved Serb-Albanian divide after the war.

slides.title: Outcome and Legacy
slides.cap: Visual reference for Outcome and Legacy.
slides.body: Yugoslav forces withdrew and Kosovo came under UN administration and NATO-led security. Kosovo later declared independence, but Serbia rejects it, leaving the war's political legacy unresolved.
